Technique Name: Obfuscated Files or Information: HTML Smuggling
Detection Criteria: `msedge.exe` / `chrome.exe` writes `%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\cert_bundle.txt` without issuing a corresponding HTTP GET request for the file
Red Team Activity: `staging.html` reconstructs `cert_bundle.txt` from base64 blob embedded in the HTML; no server request for the file

Technique Name: User Execution: Malicious Copy and Paste
Detection Criteria: `explorer.exe` spawns `powershell.exe` with command line containing `-w h -ep bypass -c "iex(gc -Raw ...)"` (indicates Win+R Run execution)
Red Team Activity: Lure page pre-loads PowerShell one-liner into clipboard; user instructed to open Win+R, paste, and press Enter

Detection Criteria: `powershell.exe` executes with arguments `-w h -ep bypass -c "iex(gc -Raw '...\cert_bundle.txt')"`
Red Team Activity: User pastes and runs the PowerShell command from Win+R

Detection Criteria: `powershell.exe` reads `%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\cert_bundle.txt`, reconstructs base64 from PEM lines, and decodes via `Security.Cryptography.FromBase64Transform` into a memory stream (follow-on file write to `%TEMP%`)
Red Team Activity: Primary scored decode step: aligns with Windows detection guidance (process + script + staged file read/write chain)

Detection Criteria: `powershell.exe` writes `%TEMP%\hpsolutionsportal.bin` and renames it to `%TEMP%\hpsolutionsportal.hta`
Red Team Activity: Payload written with `.bin` extension before rename to `.hta` to mask file type during staging; filename `hpsolutionsportal` chosen to resemble a legitimate portal application

Detection Criteria: `powershell.exe` spawns `mshta.exe` with `%TEMP%\hpsolutionsportal.hta` as argument
Red Team Activity: PowerShell executes `mshta.exe` against the dropped HTA file

Detection Criteria: `powershell.exe` reads and executes script content from `%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\cert_bundle.txt` (mismatched `.txt` extension)
Red Team Activity: **Scored** masquerade row: MIME/extension imply certificate bundle while interpreter treats content as PowerShell; richest single artifact tie-in among **T1027.013 / T1036.008 / T1140** for file metadata + execution correlation

Technique Name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
Detection Criteria: `mshta.exe` executes embedded VBScript from `hpsolutionsportal.hta`; script instantiates `MSXML2.XMLHTTP`, `ADODB.Stream`, `Scripting.FileSystemObject`, and `Shell.Application` COM objects to fetch, write, rename, and execute binaries
Red Team Activity: HTA embeds VBScript that runs within `mshta.exe`; script-host execution telemetry is independent of file creation (T1105) — detection axis is interpreter execution vs. file I/O

Detection Criteria: `mshta.exe` writes binary content to `C:\ProgramData\CertCA.bin` and `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\CertEnrollAgent.bin` via `ADODB.Stream.SaveToFile`
Red Team Activity: HTA dropper fetches and drops dnscat2 beacon and Herpaderping loader to disk

Technique Name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
Detection Criteria: `mshta.exe` creates `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\CertEnrollAgent.bin`, renamed to `CertEnrollAgent.exe` — path and name associated with legitimate Windows Certificate Enrollment components
Red Team Activity: Herpaderping loader placed under `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\` with `CertEnrollAgent.exe` name mimicking Windows certificate enrollment service; detection axis distinct from T1105 (file creation)

Detection Criteria: `mshta.exe` connects to `upload.testlab.local:80` via HTTP; GET requests to `/uploads/dnscat2.exe` and `/uploads/CWLHerpaderping.exe` issued before file creation events
Red Team Activity: HTA VBScript uses `MSXML2.XMLHTTP` to perform outbound HTTP GET requests from victim workstation to `upload.testlab.local` to fetch dnscat2 and Herpaderping loader — distinct detection axis from T1105 (file creation event)

Detection Criteria: `node.exe` writes or appends 2,000-char chunks to `C:\Windows\Temp\CertEnrollSvc.b64` via `fs.writeFileSync` and `fs.appendFileSync`
Red Team Activity: `upload` command transfers CertEnrollSvc.exe encoded as base64 in chunks via eval-based `fs` writes — no child process spawned

Detection Criteria: `node.exe` reads `C:\Windows\Temp\CertEnrollSvc.b64` and writes decoded bytes to `C:\Windows\Temp\CertEnrollSvc.bin`, followed by `fs.renameSync` rename to `C:\Windows\Temp\CertEnrollSvc.exe`
Red Team Activity: `decode` command decodes base64 file to PE bytes using Node.js `Buffer` API via eval, then `rename` moves the staged `.bin` to `.exe` — no spawn

Detection Criteria: `CertEnrollSvc.exe` elevates its token to `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM` via Named Pipe Impersonation to spawn a highly privileged child process
Red Team Activity: CertEnrollSvc uses `SeImpersonatePrivilege` held by the AppPool identity to impersonate the SYSTEM token via MS-EFSR named pipe coercion

Detection Criteria: `CertEnrollAgent.exe` maps a `SEC_IMAGE` section from a temporary file and spawns a ghost process via `NtCreateProcessEx` before overwriting the temp file on disk
Red Team Activity: CWLHerpaderping uses the Process Herpaderping technique: writes dnscat2 payload to temp file, maps `NtCreateSection(SEC_IMAGE)`, spawns ghost process via `NtCreateProcessEx` from that section, then overwrites the temp file with junk — process runs from in-memory section while on-disk file is corrupted

Technique Name: Access Token Manipulation: Parent PID Spoofing
Detection Criteria: `CertEnrollAgent.exe` spawns a ghost process with a spoofed parent PID (PPID) pointing to `svchost.exe` or `wininit.exe` in Session 0
Red Team Activity: `GetNonJobParent()` iterates `svchost.exe` then `wininit.exe` as fallback, filtering to Session 0 via `ProcessIdToSessionId`; opens first match with `PROCESS_CREATE_PROCESS` and passes handle to `NtCreateProcessEx`; token fixup overrides inherited parent token with SYSTEM

Detection Criteria: `CertEnrollAgent.exe` deletes `C:\ProgramData\CertCA.bin` from disk
Red Team Activity: CWLHerpaderping deletes the dnscat2 payload file from disk after reading it to memory to remove forensic evidence

Technique Name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
Detection Criteria: `CertEnrollAgent.exe` spawns a ghost process with the spoofed `ImageFileName` of `C:\Windows\System32\RuntimeBroker.exe`
Red Team Activity: CWLHerpaderping spawns ghost process with spoofed image path to blend with legitimate Windows processes

Detection Criteria: `RuntimeBroker.exe` (dnscat2 ghost process) issues a high volume of DNS queries containing encoded subdomain labels to `attacker.local`
Red Team Activity: dnscat2 C2 session established from IIS server as SYSTEM via Herpaderping ghost process; bootstrapped from a single react2shell session via eval detached spawn of CertEnrollSvc

Detection Criteria: `RuntimeBroker.exe` (dnscat2 ghost process) reads the `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces\{GUID}\NameServer` registry key via `RegOpenKeyEx` API
Red Team Activity: dnscat2 enumerates all TCP/IP interface GUIDs and reads `NameServer` / `DhcpNameServer` registry values to discover the DNS resolver for C2 domain tunneling

Detection Criteria: `CertEnrollSvc.exe` spawns `CertEnrollAgent.exe` with the `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (`0x08000000`) flag; `dnscat2.exe` executes without a console window
Red Team Activity: `CertEnrollSvc.exe` calls `CreateProcessAsUser` with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (`0x08000000`) to launch `CertEnrollAgent.exe` as SYSTEM; dnscat2 compiled with `-H windowsgui` — no visible window artifact on IIS server at any point during or after escalation

Detection Criteria: `CertEnrollAgent.exe` patches the remote PEB `ProcessParameters` pointer of the ghost process to a spoofed structure
Red Team Activity: `CWLHerpaderping` (`CertEnrollAgent.exe` running as SYSTEM on IIS01) builds fake `RTL_USER_PROCESS_PARAMETERS` with `RuntimeBroker.exe` image path and patches the ghost PEB pointer — process appears as a legitimate Windows component to any tool querying `ProcessParameters`

Detection Criteria: `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0)` + `Process32NextW` loop issued by `WdiBoot.exe` to locate LSASS PID; target name `lsass.exe` absent from binary strings
Red Team Activity: `QueryProcessEntry()` enumerates all running processes via toolhelp snapshot to obtain lsass PID; process name assembled at runtime as a `wchar_t` array

Detection Criteria: `WdiBoot.exe` invokes `RtlCreateProcessReflection` to clone `lsass.exe` and writes an XOR-encrypted minidump to `C:\Windows\Temp\f.elif`
Red Team Activity: ReflectDump forks LSASS via `RtlCreateProcessReflection`, dumps the fork via `MiniDumpWriteDump` with `IoWriteAllCallback` into 75 MB heap buffer, XOR-encrypts buffer in-place with key `0x35` via `XorBuffer`, then flushes to `f.elif`; reflection terminated after dump

Technique Name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
Detection Criteria: `WdiBoot.exe` writes `C:\Windows\Temp\f.elif` with entire minidump buffer XOR-encrypted using single-byte key `0x35`; file on disk contains no MDMP magic bytes or recognisable credential strings — appears as opaque binary noise to static scanners
Red Team Activity: ReflectDump XOR-encrypts entire 75 MB dump buffer in-place via `XorBuffer` with hardcoded key `0x35` before `WriteFile`; encryption applied to obfuscate LSASS memory dump content and evade signature-based detection of minidump format

Technique Name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
Detection Criteria: PE at `C:\Windows\Temp\WdiBoot.exe`; output artefact at `C:\Windows\Temp\f.elif` lacks `.dmp` extension
Red Team Activity: ReflectDump staged as `WdiBoot.exe` (mimics Windows Diagnostics Infrastructure component); dump written as `f.elif` to suppress extension-based detection rules

Detection Criteria: `node.exe` transmits the contents of `f.elif` via multiple 8,192-byte HTTP POST responses to the attacker
Red Team Activity: react2shell `download` command exfiltrates `f.elif` as base64 in 8,192-byte chunks over successive HTTP responses

Technique Name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash
Detection Criteria: `go-thehash.exe` authenticates as `TESTLAB\Administrator` to DC01 over NTLM, generating Event ID 4624 (Logon Type 3, `LogonProcessName: NtLmSsp`) on DC01 from source IP `10.12.10.20`
Red Team Activity: `go-thehash.exe` authenticates to DC01 via raw NT hash (`41c46bf74ec071f65c7b97df4b7d672a`) passed directly to `spnego.NTLMInitiator`; NTLMv2 challenge-response built in Go without touching Windows SSPI or credential store

Detection Criteria: `go-thehash.exe` accesses the `\\DC01\C$` admin share from IIS01 over SMB2 using `TESTLAB\Administrator`
Red Team Activity: `go-thehash.exe put` uses an authenticated SMB2 session to reach the `C$` admin share on DC01 with the recovered domain admin hash

Detection Criteria: `go-thehash.exe` stages `CertCA.bin` and `CertEnrollAgent.exe` at `C:\ProgramData\` on DC01 for later execution
Red Team Activity: `go-thehash.exe put` moves the dnscat2 payload (`CertCA.bin`) and Herpaderping loader (`CertEnrollAgent.exe`) from compromised IIS01 to DC01; this staging outcome is distinct from the SMB admin-share transport captured by T1021.002

Detection Criteria: `wmiprvse.exe` spawns `CertEnrollAgent.exe` on DC01 via a remote WMI `Win32_Process.Create` call originating from IIS01
Red Team Activity: `go-thehash.exe exec-wmi` calls `Win32_Process.Create(CommandLine="C:\ProgramData\CertEnrollAgent.exe")` via `IWbemServices::ExecMethod`; `wmiprvse.exe` impersonates `TESTLAB\Administrator` (DCOM impersonation) so the spawned process inherits domain admin token

Detection Criteria: `go-thehash.exe` generates Event ID 7045 on DC01 by creating a temporary service (`<random12>`) via MS-SCMR to execute `C:\ProgramData\CertEnrollAgent.exe` as `LocalSystem`
Red Team Activity: `go-thehash.exe exec` issues `RCreateServiceW` + `RStartServiceW` + `RDeleteServiceW` via the `\svcctl` named pipe; SCM spawns `CertEnrollAgent.exe` as `LocalSystem` — SCM does not impersonate the remote caller

Technique Name: Event Triggered Execution: Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription
Detection Criteria: Event ID 5861 on DC01 (`Microsoft-Windows-WMI-Activity/Operational`): consumer `CertPolicyConsumer` bound to filter `CertPolicyFilter` in `root\subscription`; `__EventFilter`, `CommandLineEventConsumer`, and `__FilterToConsumerBinding` objects queryable via `Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\subscription`
Red Team Activity: Three WMI objects created in `root\subscription`: 60-second `Win32_PerfRawData_PerfOS_System` poll filter, `CommandLineEventConsumer` pointing to `C:\ProgramData\dnscat2.exe`, and binding; `wmiprvse.exe` spawns `dnscat2.exe` directly on each poll cycle

Technique Name: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification
Detection Criteria: `scripts.ini` created or modified under `C:\Windows\SYSVOL\sysvol\testlab.local\Policies\{31B2F340-016D-11D2-945F-00C04FB984F9}\User\Scripts\`; file-write event on SYSVOL path by a process outside normal GPO management tools (`gpmc.msc`, `Set-GPO`); DFS-R replication propagates the change to all DCs within minutes
Red Team Activity: Attacker writes `scripts.ini` directly into the Default Domain Policy SYSVOL path from the DC01 SYSTEM shell — modifying the live GPO content without using any Group Policy management interface; workstations pick up the modified policy on next logon and execute `update.exe` (dnscat2) via `userinit.exe`

Technique Name: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts: Network Logon Script
Detection Criteria: On domain-joined workstation: `userinit.exe` spawns `update.exe` (resolved from `\\testlab.local\SYSVOL\...`) during domain user logon; Sysmon Event 1: `ParentImage = C:\Windows\System32\userinit.exe`, `Image = update.exe`
Red Team Activity: GPO logon script execution: `userinit.exe` reads `scripts.ini` and launches `update.exe` (dnscat2) in the logged-on user's security context; execution originates from a legitimate Windows process — not from a ghost or injected context
